excerpt: மாலை உடனே பாமாலை புனைந்தே விடிகாலை அந்தி

sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
மாலை உடனே பாமாலை புனைந்தே விடிகாலை அந்தி
மாலைத் திருமாலை நினைந்தே பணி
sections.translit:
mAlai udanE pAmAlai punaindhE vidikAlai andhi
mAlaith thirumAlai ninaindhE paNi
sections.en: Every day at dawn and dusk, think of Lord Vishnu’s name and worship him with a garland of flowers, as well as a garland of poetic words.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
பாலைக் கடைந்த தூயன் கனித்தோலை ஏற்ற நேயன்
கோலை தரித்த ஆயன் சேலை நெய்த மாயன் நாமம் ஜபி
sections.translit:
pAlaik kadaindha thUyan kanitthOlai EtRa nEyan
kOlai dharittha Ayan sElai neidha mAyan nAmam jabi
sections.en: He is the immaculate one who churned the milky ocean. As a good friend of Vidura, he accepted the skin of a fruit offered to Him. Vidura, dazzled by the radiance of His divine face, forgot that he threw away the fruit’s pulp and offered Him only peels. Lord Vishnu carried a wooden stick in his hand in his incarnation as a shepherd. He even wove a sari when a damsel in distress called out his name, asking for help.  Chant His divine name.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
மின்னல் இடியோடு அடைமழை பெய்யக் குல
இன்னல் போக்கியது போல் உன்துயர் பொடிக்கும்
அண்ணலின் திருப் பெயரைக் கருத்தினில் இருத்தி
எண்ணலின் பெரிதொன்றுண்டோ இந்தத் தாரணி தனிலே
sections.translit:
minnal idiyOdu adaimazhai peyyak kula
innal pOkkiyadhu pOl unthuyar podikkum
aNNalin thirup peyaraik karutthinil irutthi
eNNalin peridhondRuNdO indhath thAraNi thanilE
sections.en: Is there anything greater than retaining His name in your thoughts and chanting it repeatedly each day? He will remove your sorrow just as he alleviated the troubles of his shepherd clan through torrential rainfall.

notes: Lines 1 and 2 of the charanam refer to Krishna protecting his shepherd clan from the wrath of Lord Indra by lifting the Govardhana Mountain with his finger and wielding it like an umbrella, so that the fierce rainfall would not hurt them. ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், இரண்டாம் பாகம், உரை ஆசிரியர் அண்ணா, ஶ்ரீராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 600004, கோவர்த்தனோத்தரணம், பக்கம் 71-77. The anupallavi refers to the divine acts of Lord Vishnu. The first half of Line 1 in Anupallavi refers to samudhra manthan. Devas and asuras, based on Lord Vishnu’s recommendations, churned the milky ocean to get the elixir. Vishnu became a base of physical support for the churning process. He assumed the form of a heavy tortoise carrying the heavy Mantara mountain on his back. The Vasuki snake became the rope and the celestial beings held on to the tail. The asuras held the head of the snake and churned the ocean. ஶ்ரீ விஷ்ணு புராணம், முதல் பாகம், வெளியிடுவோர்: ஶ்ரீ ந்ருசிம்ஹப்ரியா ட்ரஸ்ட், நெ.30, வெங்கடேச அக்ரஹாரம், மைலாப்பூர்,சென்னை 600004, இரண்டாம் பதிப்பு 2003, பக்கம் 95-107. As a member of a cowherd family, Krishna was growing in the company of other children in the shepherd clan. The first half of Anupallavi Line 2 refers to his activity as a shepherd. Each day, he left with a small stick alongside cows and calves (see sloka 13.11, 13.19 page 29, 30 of the reference ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், இரண்டாம் பாகம்) to control the herd, and a flute to entertain the herd and his friends. Krishna enjoyed the company of the other kids and had fun playing his youthful pranks. All these Brindavan leelas of Krishna are described in Bhagavatam. ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், இரண்டாம் பாகம், உரை ஆசிரியர் அண்ணா, ஶ்ரீராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 600004, பிருந்தாவன லீலை, பக்கம் 22-47. During the visit to Hasthinapura –the Kaurava capital– to discuss a peace settlement with Duryodhana, Krishna turned down a request to eat at the palace. Instead, Krishna visited Vidhura’s home. Both Vidhura and his wife Sulabha did not expect this sudden visit from Krishna and did not have food at home to serve this guest. During their conversation, Vidhura picked up some bananas from the kitchen and offered them to Krishna. Mesmerized by Krishna’s charm, Vidhura peeled the banana, threw away the pulp, and offered him the peels. The second half of Line 1 of Anupallavi refers to this episode. Krishna enjoyed this offering steeped in devotion and love. Vidura’s Devotion to Krishna After the Pandavas lost their independence and their kingdom during the game of dice with the Kauravas, they also bet and lost their wife Draupadi. A venomous Duryodhana ordered Dushasana to bring her to the court and to disrobe her in the hall. A distraught Draupadi prayed to Lord Krishna and through his mystical powers, the sari that Dushasana was trying to remove became limitless. An exhausted Dushasana collapsed. This episode is referenced in the second half of Anupallavi Line 2. Mahabharata vividly describes Dushasana’s acts and Lord Krishna’s magical replenishment of the sari in the Kaurava court. ஶ்ரீ மஹாபாரத ஸாரம், உரை ஆசிரியர் அண்ணா, ஶ்ரீராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 600004, Sections 68.40 through 68.49, பக்கம் 386-8.
